conviction_note: abs_move 16 (event-implied 15.1, own median 15.0, raised slightly because a full-year cash-generation guide revision is the likely swing factor and on this repo's resolved samples the hunters' numbers have run too small) times a p_up of 47. Three negative findings push the lean down: 10y yields rose 30-60bp after the 2026-08-05 guide cut, the company needs a large H2 cash ramp to reach even the low end of the range, and peers show a 35% YoY drop in industry demand. Against them sit about 30% of shares short at 8.6 days to cover and a call skew of -28.5 vol points. All three negatives are inference or proxy rather than an unseen company number, so the lean stays near 50. The findings sum to -0.9 and the scaled number is -0.96, so the two measurements agree.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus about $757-760M and EPS $0.16-0.20 (MarketBeat $0.2009/$757.53M https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-4-sunrun-inc-stock/ ; Investing.com $0.16/$760M https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/sunrun-earnings-in-focus-as-borrowing-costs-test-solar-demand-93CH-5000225). Other sources disagree: Zacks $0.12-0.26 / $796-804M, Benzinga $0.36 / $832M (dated 2026-10-02). The bar the stock trades on is the company's FY2026 guide from 2026-08-05: Cash Generation $200-375M excluding safe harbor (cut from $250-450M) and Aggregate Subscriber Value $4.6-4.9B (cut from $4.8-5.2B) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026053349/exhibit991q226.htm . The revenue/EPS bar is disputed between sources, so the reported-quarter findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 71.66M shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, 8.6 days to cover, against 240.85M shares outstanding, about 29.8% of shares out (https://massive.com/quote/run , snapshot 2026-11-04). The 2026-09-30 settlement showed 70.7M short and 8.9 days to cover. Chartmill gives 28.1% of float, undated. Skew -28.53 vol points (25d put IV minus 25d call IV) means calls are paid over puts, and put/call OI is 0.19. Run-up was +19.6% over 5d and +16.6% over 20d off a 52-week low of $6.78, on a sector rebound and easing yields (247wallst 2026-11-03). Today the stock opened $9.36, hit $9.93 intraday and faded to ~$8.9 on 18.9M shares by 13:06 ET, about 2.3x average. This is a crowded short with the option market leaning up.

findings.finding: Rates moved against the capital-cost assumption behind the 2026-08-05 guide cut. The 10-year Treasury was 4.70% on 2026-08-03, when the CFO cut FY Cash Generation to $200-375M partly for 'modestly higher capital costs'. It then rose to 5.00% on 09-15, 5.24% on 09-28 and a 5.31% close on 10-05, and eased to 5.00% on 10-23. Q3 and early Q4 project finance was therefore priced 30-60bp above the guide's rate deck, and an analyst flagged roughly 50bp higher 7-year yields as 'a headwind to 2026 cash generation guidance'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance lines drive this name. The 2026-02-26 print, with the outlook as the focus, went -35.1%. The 2026-08-05 print cut the cash generation and subscriber value guides on a large revenue/EPS beat and went -10.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Goldman ($13 to $11), Citi ($16 to $14), Morgan Stanley ($15 to $10) and Mizuho ($18 to $15) cut targets in October citing near-term cash generation, and the stock hit $6.78. Since then it has rallied 20% in 5 sessions on the yield easing, and the call skew is bid, so the market is pricing relief rather than a further guide cut. If the market had priced a cut, the stock would not be 28% off its low with calls bid into the print.
findings.independence: The headwind call is from an Investing.com preview (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/sunrun-earnings-in-focus-as-borrowing-costs-test-solar-demand-93CH-5000225, 2026-11-04). The CFO's own capital-cost reason is in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026053349/exhibit991q226.htm). This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed for Q3. A partial offset is that ABS spreads tightened 20bp in the August deal (200bp vs 220bp in April) per https://investors.sunrun.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/377 .

findings.finding: The FY2026 Cash Generation guide needs an H2 that looks large against everything since the cut. H1 2026 Cash Generation excluding safe harbor was about $14M (Q1 -$31M, Q2 +$45M). Holding the $200-375M guide therefore requires $186-361M in H2. H2 2025 delivered $295M (Q3 $108M, which included a third-party system sale, and Q4 $187M) on Q3 2025 subscriber additions of 30,104. 2026 additions are running 25-31% lower (Q1 17,665, Q2 19,793) and capital costs are higher. The midpoint ($273M H2) needs roughly 2025's H2 on about 30% less volume. The company itself expects direct volume to return to YoY growth in Q3 and grow more than 10% in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same guidance line as above. The Q2 2026 cash-generation cut produced -10.6% despite a 16% revenue beat. Q3 2025 reported $108M of cash generation with the guide unchanged at the midpoint and the stock fell 16.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Every number is public, but the H2 arithmetic is not in any preview found. Previews quote the range, and TIKR (2026-10-09) treats $200-375M as a support level whose breach would pressure targets. If the market expected a cut to below $200M, the stock would not have rallied 20% into the print with calls bid.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release with the rates finding but rests on a different fact: volume and H1 cash, not rates. Q1 figures are from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026031259/exhibit991q126.htm . Q3 2025 figures are from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1469367/000162828025050170/exhibit991q325.htm . The guide cut has one cause in the rates finding and one here, so together they argue for the low end or a cut, and they are kept small because Q4 is seasonally the heavy cash quarter.

findings.finding: Counterparties that reported after Sunrun last spoke show US residential demand down sharply. Enphase (2026-10-27) reported Q3 US sell-through -35% YoY and cited third-party data with US residential permits down about 35% YoY in Q3. It guided Q4 sell-through down another 10% sequentially, with Q4 revenue at a $240M midpoint against $298.6M consensus, and its CEO sees 'no meaningful recovery'. SolarEdge (2026-11-04) guided Q4 revenue to $245-275M from $326.1M in Q3, citing 'softer demand'. Enphase is also scaling its own Propel prepaid-lease TPO product: 350 installers and more than 300 weekly originations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber additions fell 25% (Q1) and 31% (Q2) YoY. The Q1 print went +7.6% and the Q2 print -10.6%, so the volume line by itself has not set the sign; the guide did.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. RUN fell about 5% to ~$7 on the Enphase print, and then rallied 27% from there on rates and a sector bounce that 24/7 Wall St says is 'not driven by fundamentals alone'. The SolarEdge Q4 guide came out this morning and RUN still trades up about 2-3% on the day.
findings.independence: SolarEdge Q3 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001419612/000117891326004999/exhibit_99-1.htm (2026-11-04). Enphase call: https://www.webull.com/news/15824347536306176 . This is an industry proxy, and Sunrun's TPO model partly benefits from the 25D expiry shifting demand to leases and PPAs (EnergySage: TPO quoting installers rose from 14% to 41%, Jan-Jun 2026, https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/10/24/residential-solar-prices-rise-3-2-as-third-party-ownership-gains-ground/). The net is sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: The print turns on a company-stated volume test: on the Q2 call management said direct-business volume resumes YoY growth in Q3 and grows more than 10% YoY in H2. Affiliate installations are expected down more than 60% for the year (partner Freedom Forever went bankrupt), direct sales are expected to exceed 85% of origination, and more than 1,500 sales reps were hired year to date. Q3 total subscriber additions of about 30,104 in Q3 2025 set the YoY comparison. The direction is undetermined from public data.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume misses have come bundled with guide cuts (2026-08-05, -10.6%). A volume line inside the company's own Q3 expectation is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither direction can be priced because there is no public Q3 Sunrun volume datapoint. The industry permit series (-35%) and the company's own 'direct returns to growth' claim point opposite ways, which is why this sits at 0.
findings.independence: Hiring: https://cleantechnica.com/2026/08/20/sunrun-shifts-away-from-affiliates-to-direct-sales/ . The CFO's H2 >10% direct-growth claim is repeated in TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/goldman-sachs-cut-its-sunrun-target-it-still-sees-44-upside, 2026-10-09).

findings.finding: The short is crowded and the option market leans up into the print. 71.66M shares were short as of the 2026-10-15 settlement (about 29.8% of 240.85M shares outstanding) at 8.6 days to cover, up from 64.7M on 08-19. The 25-delta skew is -28.5 vol points, so calls are richer than puts, and put/call OI is 0.19. The stock ran +19.6% in 5 sessions off a $6.78 52-week low into the print, on 2.3x normal volume today. A print that avoids a cash-generation cut gives a squeeze mechanism with 8.6 days of cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The upside reactions on this name are large: +32.3% (2025-08-06), +15.0% (2025-05-07) and +7.6% (2026-05-06), consistent with short covering. But 4 of the last 7 prints fell, by 8-35%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 5-day run-up is itself covering, and today's fade from $9.93 to $8.9 suggests some of the rally was sold into. Short interest was still near its highs at the last settlement, so most of the short has not covered.
findings.independence: The skew and put/call figures come from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options, 2026-11-04 18:09 UTC), a different source from the short-interest data. Earlier short interest (64.7M, 7.2 days to cover, 2026-08-19) is from https://equibles.com/stocks/run/shortinterest .

findings.finding: The reported-quarter bar has been cut. EPS estimates fell more than 20% over the two months to 2026-11-04, and the revenue consensus is about $757-760M against $870M reported in Q2 and $724.6M in Q3 2025. Sunrun beat Q2 revenue by 16% ($870.0M vs $746.9M) and EPS by $0.19, and Q1 by $0.67. A headline beat is the likely outcome, but this name has sold its headline beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat revenue by 16% and EPS by 83% and the stock went -10.6%. Q3 2025 was reported as 'strong' and went -16.1%. Q1 2026 beat and went +7.6%. Headline beats do not set the sign here.
findings.why_not_priced: The lowered bar is in the wire and therefore priced. What is not priced is the size of the beat: revenue includes lumpy product and system sales ($326M in Q2, +193%), which are not in a run-rate consensus. The bar is disputed between sources ($757M to $832M), so this is capped small.

findings.finding: Grid-services evidence is building. Sunrun's California home batteries delivered a record 745 MW on 2026-10-06 (the prior record was 580 MW on 09-09). Its Puerto Rico distributed power plant doubled to more than 60,000 customers and dispatched for 18 consecutive days from 10-13. This supports the Tesla/Renew Home 16 GW flexible-capacity narrative from June.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 Tesla/Renew Home partnership produced a +13-22% day outside a print. Grid-services revenue has not been a print line before.
findings.why_not_priced: These are company press releases and therefore public. The only thing not priced is whether management attaches a revenue or contracted-value figure to it on the call; nothing found says it will.
findings.independence: Puerto Rico release: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/03/3394183/0/en/sunrun-doubles-puerto-rico-distributed-power-plant-participation-as-grid-operator-calls-on-home-batteries-to-help-prevent-outages.html (2026-11-03). It is the same company as source, so not independent.

findings.finding: Tesla, Sunrun's main battery supplier, deployed 13.7 GWh of storage in Q3 2026, 14% below its own compiled consensus of 15.9 GWh: flat sequentially and +10% YoY. Storage revenue fell 16% YoY. No residential Powerwall split was disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history of RUN reacting to Tesla storage data at its own print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced and mostly Megapack. It is a weak read-through to residential, filed only for breadth.
findings.independence: https://www.energy-storage.news/tesla-q3-2026-energy-storage-revenues-fall-despite-second-highest-quarterly-deployments/ (could not fetch, 403). This is a proxy, and Sunrun's own storage attach rate was a record 74% in Q2.

findings.finding: Insider Form 4 filings on 2026-10-07 (President/CRO Paul Dickson 15,837 shares, CFO Danny Abajian 16,734, Jeanna Steele 10,042 and others, at about $7.76 on 10-06) are sales to cover tax on vested RSUs, on the same quarterly pattern as the July filings. There are no 10b5-1 or discretionary sales and no insider buying.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine sales with no information content, filed at zero for completeness.
findings.independence: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-sunrun-nasdaq-run-stock-price-down-49-should-you-sell-2026-10-19/ (describes the same sales as tax-withholding sales).

findings.finding: Sunrun filed a Form D (Rule 506(b)) on 2026-09-11 for an equity / option-to-acquire offering with a total offering amount of '100', nothing sold and first sale on 2026-09-08. It looks like a nominal warrant or option instrument, possibly tied to a partnership, and is not a capital raise.
findings.why_not_priced: It is unexplained in any public text found. The 10-Q may describe a warrant issued to a partner. The financing question 'what does the money buy' has no answer here because the amount is nominal, so it is sized at zero.

outside_window.finding: Treasury is required to publish additional FEOC safe-harbor tables by 2026-12-31. The 48E FEOC material-assistance threshold is 40% for 2026 construction starts and rises 5 points a year, which bears on Sunrun's 2027 TPO cost basis.

baseline_tension: The evidence cuts against the baseline. My filed facts lean mildly negative on the guide (rates, H2 cash arithmetic, industry demand), while the skew (-28.5, calls paid), the +19.6% 5-day run-up and the ~30% short interest all lean up. So the negatives were shrunk and p_up sits at 47, not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning): with short interest ~30% and a -28.5 call skew, the two guidance negatives were shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0 each, and p_up moved from 45 to 47.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs document): the Enphase/SolarEdge industry-demand finding is a proxy partly offset by the TPO shift after the 25D expiry; it went from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 6 (bar): consensus revenue/EPS is disputed between sources ($757M-$832M, $0.12-$0.36), so the reported-quarter beat finding stays capped at +0.3.
Lesson 1 (verified fact vs reaction): headline beats have been sold (Q2 beat, -10.6%), so the beat finding was left small and the guide is treated as the line that decides the sign.
Lesson 3 (read the set): the rates and H2-cash findings both point at the guide but rest on different facts, so both are kept and the shared-document overlap is stated in independence.
